analysis_error.invalid_json: The answer of the model could not be parsed as JSON.
baseline.disabled: baseline is disabled in the settings (llm.baseline.enabled=false)
baseline.no_service: the service of the run is not set
baseline.no_storage: the metrics storage is not used for this run
baseline.read_error: failed to read the baseline from the database: {error}
context_import.system: You transfer the description of a software system from a document into a JSON structure. Use only the information from the document and return only JSON.
forecast.system: You are a performance engineer. Answer strictly in JSON of the given schema, all texts in English.
guidance.domain_sla_step: - The target RPS and the maximum throughput are checked programmatically on the step from sla_step. Do not assess them from the metrics of this domain and do not compare the RPS of services with target_rps.
guidance.header: ANALYSIS GUIDANCE (generated automatically from the service settings):
guidance.metric_no_data: no data in this run — do not quote values
guidance.metric_unknown: - When the meaning or the unit of a query is not set, judge the metric by its name and note only; do not guess the unit.
guidance.metrics_title: DOMAIN METRICS (the configured queries; a section in sections[] has the same name as its query):
guidance.min_stable: - Minimum duration of a stable step: {minutes} min
guidance.only_source: - The only source of numeric thresholds is this block and deterministic_sla in the context. Do not use norms that are not here.
guidance.peak_fallback_allowed: - If stable_max is missing, the peak max may be used for target_rps
guidance.peak_fallback_forbidden: - If stable_max is missing, using the peak max for target_rps is FORBIDDEN
guidance.rule_normal: - Considered normal (do not lower the verdict for it): {rule}
guidance.rule_risk: - Known risk (check it against the data): {rule}
guidance.rules_title: Customer rules from the system description:
guidance.sla_scope: - Each threshold applies only to its own query. Do not compare other metrics with it: the mean processing time of a service is not the p95 of the load tool, process CPU is not node CPU.
guidance.sla_source_none: no query selected, not checked programmatically
guidance.soak_domain: - The target RPS and the load hold are checked programmatically on the hold window (hold_window). Do not assess them from the metrics of this domain and do not compare the RPS of services with target_rps.
guidance.soak_target: - The target RPS of a soak test is the level to hold for the whole test: it is checked programmatically against the mean and the minimum RPS of the hold window{source} (hold_window, stability_under_load).
guidance.soak_thresholds: - The latency, error and resource thresholds are checked on the hold window, without the ramp-up. Degradation towards the end of the test is a violation even if the target level was reached at the start.
guidance.spike_domain: - The target RPS and the recovery are checked programmatically in the spike windows (spike_windows). Do not assess them from the metrics of this domain and do not compare the RPS of services with target_rps.
guidance.spike_target: - The target RPS of a spike test is the spike level: it is checked programmatically in the spike window (spike_analysis).
guidance.spike_thresholds: - The latency and error thresholds are checked in the spike windows; the recovery after a spike is a separate criterion, recovery.
guidance.stack_title: Stack metric specifics (from the installed query packs):
guidance.target_reached: - The target_rps criterion is met when a step at the target RPS holds the latency and error thresholds (deterministic_sla.target_rps_check, target_window), even if degradation followed.
guidance.target_step: - The CPU and memory thresholds are checked programmatically on the target step (sla_step with a role, deterministic_sla.target_window): the first step where target_rps is reached and the latency and error thresholds hold. Breaches on the steps above it are headroom used up (deterministic_sla.headroom), not a risk: do not lower the verdict because of them, describe them as headroom.
judge.system: You are an experienced load testing engineer acting as an independent judge. Use the provided metric context to assess the candidates impartially. Return only JSON as requested.
peak.designated: The ONLY source of peak_performance.max_rps. Do NOT use the RPS of the microservices domain to determine the maximum throughput of the system.
peak.not_applicable: peak_performance does not apply to the "{test}" test. {focus}
rationale.derived_findings:
Verdict "{label}" is based on the key observations of the report.
{bullets}
rationale.derived_no_data: Verdict "{label}": the available metrics are not enough for a confident assessment.
rationale.derived_other: Verdict "{label}" is based on the available metrics and the risks found.
rationale.derived_pass: Verdict "{label}": no significant deviations were found in the available data.
rationale.head_fail: Status "{label}": according to the confirmed data the target result of the test is not reached.
rationale.head_no_data: Status "{label}": the answer has no sufficient confirmed facts.
rationale.head_pass: Status "{label}": the confirmed metrics show no significant deviations.
rationale.head_risk: Status "{label}": there are confirmed deviations, but the target result is not failed.
system.structured: You are a load testing engineer. Analyze the results of the load test from the user's data and fill in the answer structure. All text fields in English.
verdict.final_adjusted: The final verdict is adjusted by deterministic_sla: for the "{test}" test, CPU/memory overruns count as risks, not as a failure on their own, while the primary SLA on target RPS, error rate and latency is not violated.
verdict.sla_step_adjusted: Status adjusted by the SLA step: on step "{step}" the SLA thresholds are met, the serious problems of the domain began after it. The original assessment of the model: "{label}".
